title: CHAPTER THIRTY-TWO. On Fate
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): even if lot, chance plus fortune are sometimes found therein — plus in sacred Scripture you will not find ye name Fate — as Anaxagoras, with Alexander witnessing in ye book concerning Fate plus ye second concerning ye soul — who gave God ye world's generation plus ye distinction plus regimen belonging toward things — Moreover even more ancient philosophers say ye name belonging toward fate is vain plus false. in which Doctor Gregory agrees with him — because he says this was given toward ye stars by Astrologers — But yet he thinks ye name belonging toward fate is to be exploded. as if those things which happen by fate were ordered plus decreed by someone speaking plus commanding — Whence fate is said from speaking, with Blessed Augustine witnessing. as necessity toward power giving each one to be according toward its mode — plus to pertain toward ordering wisdom — because fate itself seems to be in ye concurrence belonging toward many things — differing from necessity which seems chiefly to consist in simple things plus things considered alone. Therefore ye SECOND great influx put into things is Fate. FATE is ye great influx belonging toward divine wisdom granting things a mode by which in causing they are ordered toward one another. CHAPTER THIRTY-TWO. On Fate.
pass_b_english: FATE is the great influx of divine wisdom granting things a mode by which in causing they are ordered toward one another. Therefore the SECOND great influx put into things is Fate, differing from necessity — which seems chiefly to consist in simple things considered alone — inasmuch as fate itself seems to be in the concurrence of many things and to pertain to ordering wisdom, as necessity pertains to power giving each thing to be according to its mode.

Whence fate is said from speaking (fari), as Blessed Augustine witnesses, as if the things that happen by fate were ordered and decreed by someone speaking and commanding. Yet he thinks the name of fate ought to be exploded, because he says this was given to the stars by the Astrologers — in which Doctor Gregory agrees with him. Moreover even the more ancient philosophers who gave God the world's generation and the distinction and regimen of things say the name of fate is vain and false, as Anaxagoras, Alexander witnessing in the book On Fate and the second On the Soul; and in sacred Scripture you will not find the name Fate, even if lot, chance, and fortune are sometimes found there.
source_text: CAPUT TRICESIMUM SECUNDUM, De Fato. FATUM est magnus divinae sapientiae influxus largiens rebus modum, quo in causando ad se invicem ordinantur. SECUNDUS ergo magnus influxus rebus inditus est Fatum, differens a necessitate, quae potissimum consistere videtur in rebus simplicibus et solitarie consideratis, eo quod ipsum fatum videtur esse in rerum multarum concursu, et pertinere ad sapientiam ordinantem, sicuti necessitas ad potentiam dantem unicuique esse iuxta modum suum. Unde fatum dicitur a fando, teste B. Augustino, quasi quae fato fiunt, ab aliquo dicente ac iubente ordinata ac decreta sint. Sed tamen nomen fati explodendum putat, quia dicit hoc datum esse sideribus ab Astrologis, in quo ei adstipulatur D. Gregorius. Quin etiam philosophi antiquiores, qui Deo generationem mundi et distinctionem regimenque rerum dederunt, fati nomen vanum esse falsumque dicunt, ut Anaxagoras, teste Alexandro libro de Fato et secundo de anima; et in sacra Scriptura non invenies nomen Fati, etiamsi sors, casus et fortuna inibi interdum inveniatur.
